html:
Alice Lenshina was a Bemba prophet who founded the Lumpa Church in northern Zambia in the 1950s, after she said she had died and returned with a message from God.

Thousands joined her church, which banned witchcraft, alcohol and polygamy and sang hymns in Bemba. At its height it had tens of thousands of members, drawn away from the mission churches.

Lumpa members refused to join politics, including Kaunda's party. In 1964, just before independence, clashes between her followers and party supporters turned into war, and troops killed hundreds of Lumpa members. The church was banned and Lenshina was held in detention for years. It was the first great crisis of independent Zambia, and a sign of the strength of African Christianity.
sum: Alice Lenshina was a Bemba prophet who founded the Lumpa Church in northern Zambia in the 1950s, after she said she had died and returned with a message from God.
